title: Which unit can you take? The mill-protection rule, shown on a real Millfall match
text:
A rule that decides a lot of games: when you close a mill, you can't take an enemy unit that is standing in a closed mill of its own. You must take one outside a mill. The only exception: if every enemy unit stands in a mill, any of them can be taken.

The GIF is from a real Millfall match (Moss Grove): Dusk closes a mill, five of Dawn's seven units stand in two mills, so only two can be taken, and the engine's execution hits one of those two. Both sides are played by the game's own AI.

Millfall on the Microsoft Store (Windows PC): https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NHQ64JTDQV2?cid=rd

title: He fell up: the gravity execution in Millfall, from a real AI vs AI match
text:
In Millfall (pixel-art Nine Men's Morris), closing a mill means your unit executes an enemy unit, and warriors and mages each have their own executions. This one is Gravity: in a Star Shrine match, the Dawn mage Garbald places the third piece of a mill, and the Dusk unit Mormir lifts off, tumbles and falls up out of the picture. Both sides are played by the game's own AI; recorded in-engine.

Millfall on the Microsoft Store (Windows PC): https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NHQ64JTDQV2?cid=rd
